# The Role of Integrating Strategic Management Accounting with

# Big Data and Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Financial

# Analysis and Decision-Making

Alimuddin, Asri Usman, Aulia Thalita Sada Abbas, Nuriya Fadila

Universitas Hasanuddin, Indonesia Email: alimuddin@fe.unhas.ac.id, asriusman@unhas.ac.id, auliathalitasadaabbas@gmail.com, nuriyafadila29@gmail.com

Abstrak This study aims to systematically analyze the crucial role of integrating Strategic Management Accounting with Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing financial analysis capabilities and the effectiveness of strategic decision-making. Using the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, this study synthesizes the findings of 29 relevant scientific articles indexed in the Scopus database from 2014 to 2024, identified through the keywords "strategic management accounting, big data, and artificial intelligence." The results of the analysis demonstrate that this integration fundamentally transforms financial analysis, making it more predictive, accurate, and real-time, while also accelerating and improving the quality of datadriven decision-making. Moreover, these findings reveal a shift in the role of accountants from operational functions to strategic advisors, necessitating proficiency in analytical skills and technological literacy. It can be concluded that the synergy between strategic management accounting, Big Data, and AI serves as a key driver of competitive advantage. However, its success is highly dependent on the organization's ability to address challenges such as skills gaps, ethical risks, and the critical importance of implementing robust information technology governance as an essential mediating factor. Kata kunci: Strategic Management Accounting, Big Data, Artificial Intelligence, Financial Analysis, Decision Making, IT Governance INTRODUCTION

The contemporary business world is faced with a rapidly changing environment, characterized by increasingly fierce competition, globalization, and massive technological disruption (Nguyen & Tran, 2024; Andriushchenko et al., 2019; Manrique Plácido et al., 2025). Rapid advances in Information and Communication Technology (ICT), particularly in the realm of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI), have become key drivers of digital transformation across various industrial sectors (Sánchez Toledano et al., 2024; Almaqtari, 2024; Pantea et al., 2024). This phenomenon, often referred to as the Industry 4.0 era, compels companies to continually adapt and innovate to maintain their competitive advantage and ensure business sustainability (Andriushchenko et al., 2019; Gu & Zhou, 2023). In this context, the ability to make rapid, precise, and data-driven strategic decisions is a crucial factor for organizational success (Fernández-Revuelta Pérez & Romero Blasco, 2022; Abdullah et al., 2022).

This paradigm shift places significant pressure on accounting and finance functions. Traditional management accounting models, which tend to focus on internal, historical, and aggregated data, are often considered inadequate for addressing the challenges of the modern business environment (Wang & Dai, 2025; Ren, 2022). The limitations in handling vast data volumes, the speed of market changes, and the complexity of inter-variable relationships make it difficult for conventional methods to provide relevant and timely information to decision-makers (Theodorakopoulos et al., 2024; Ren, 2022). Consequently, there is an urgent need for companies to transform their financial functions, shifting from mere transaction recording to becoming proactive strategic partners (Bian & Bian, 2022).

To address these challenges, two main concepts have emerged as pillars of transformation: Strategic Management Accounting and Big Data and AI technologies. Strategic management accounting represents a modern approach that looks not only inward (internal) but also outward (external), focusing on delivering information about both the business and its competitors to support the formulation and monitoring of long-term strategies (Nguyen & Tran, 2024). Conversely, Big Data, with its primary characteristics of volume, velocity, and variety (3V), provides an extraordinarily large resource of information that was previously inaccessible or unanalyzable using traditional tools (Theodorakopoulos et al., 2024; Abdullah et al., 2022). Enhanced by AI and machine learning algorithms, Big Data enables process automation, predictive analytics, identification of hidden patterns, and extraction of deep insights from both structured and unstructured data (Manrique Plácido et al., 2025; Liu, 2024; Jia et al., 2022; Samarghandi et al., 2023).

The most transformative impact arises from the integration of Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) frameworks with the analytical capabilities of Big Data and AI (Abdullah et al., 2022; Gu & Zhou, 2023). The application of these technologies can enhance the accuracy of cost estimation, optimize audit processes by analyzing entire data populations, improve the quality of financial reporting, and provide a robust quantitative basis for investment decisions and business strategies (Fernández-Revuelta Pérez & Romero Blasco, 2022; Almaqtari, 2024; Theodorakopoulos et al., 2024; Wang & Dai, 2025). However, this integration is not straightforward. Organizations face significant challenges, such as ensuring data quality and reliability, the need for substantial infrastructure investments, skills gaps among accounting professionals, and critical issues related to ethics, privacy, and data security that necessitate a robust and mature IT Governance framework (Theodorakopoulos et al., 2024; Pantea et al., 2024; Almaqtari, 2024; Agbon, 2024).

The role of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in transforming business strategies has been a central focus in recent studies. Nguyen & Tran (2024) and Andriushchenko et al. (2019) have highlighted how technological advancements, particularly in Big Data and AI, have driven

digital transformation across various industries. These technologies are viewed as critical enablers for modernizing traditional management accounting practices, facilitating faster and more accurate decision-making (Sánchez Toledano et al., 2024). While much of the existing literature addresses the theoretical framework of Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) and the application of Big Data and AI in accounting, there remains a gap in understanding how these concepts can be effectively integrated to address the challenges faced by modern businesses. The research by Fernández-Revuelta Pérez & Romero Blasco (2022) and Theodorakopoulos et al. (2024) explored the potential benefits of combining SMA with Big Data and AI, but did not focus on the practical difficulties organizations encounter in bridging this gap, such as infrastructure requirements, data governance, and the ethical implications of using AI in accounting.

This research addresses these gaps by conducting a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to synthesize and analyze the integration of SMA with Big Data and AI in financial decision-making. The study highlights key benefits such as improved cost estimation, enhanced audit processes, and higher-quality financial reporting, while also focusing on implementation challenges, including infrastructure, data security, and the required skill sets for professionals. The novelty of this research lies in its comprehensive analysis of both the strategic and operational challenges organizations face in adopting these technologies.

Given the complexity and strategic significance of this integration, a deep understanding of the existing research landscape is essential. Therefore, the purpose of this Systematic Literature Review (SLR) is to systematically synthesize and analyze the findings of 29 relevant academic documents. This research specifically aims to identify the key roles and benefits of integrating Strategic Management Accounting with Big Data and AI in financial analysis and decision-making processes; to map challenges, barriers, and critical considerations (including ethics and governance) in the implementation of such integrations; to present a conceptual framework emerging from the literature to understand this phenomenon; and to formulate future research agendas and directions to deepen understanding in this rapidly evolving field. RESEARCH METHOD

This study employed the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach to comprehensively analyze and synthesize existing academic literature. This methodology was selected for its capacity to identify, evaluate, and interpret all research evidence relevant to the topic in a structured, transparent, and replicable manner. The primary focus of this SLR is to map the roles, benefits, challenges, and conceptual frameworks that arise from the integration of Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) with Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI). To achieve this objective, the research method is organized into several main stages, which are detailed in the following points.

Research Object

The main object of this research is the phenomenon of integration between Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) with Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology. The focus of the research is to understand in depth the role, impact, and implications of this integration on two crucial areas in corporate management, namely the improvement of financial analysis capabilities and the effectiveness of strategic decision-making. The scope of the research includes an analysis of the benefits generated, changes in the role of the accounting profession, the theoretical frameworks used, and the challenges, risks, and accompanying governance mechanisms. Research Questions

The first step in doing Systematic Literature Review (SLR) Includes the formulation of key research questions. Technique Systematic Literature Review (SLR)  guided by research questions that establish the topic, focus, and scope of study (Snyder, 2019). This research question was made based on the needs of the selected topic, namely: RQ1: What are the key roles and benefits of the integration of Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) with Big Data and AI in improving financial analysis and decision-making? RQ2: How has this integration changed the role of management accountants as well as work processes within the organization? RQ3: What are the most significant challenges, risks, and ethical considerations in implementing this integration, and how does IT Governance play a role in managing it? Literature Search

The literature search process is carried out systematically on the Scopus database using the Publish or Perish software. The search parameters are limited to articles published within the last 10 years (January 2014 – June 2024) to ensure the relevance and novelty of the information. The keywords used in the search were a combination of: "strategic management accounting", "big data", and "artificial intelligence". This initial identification process succeeded in collecting 288 potentially relevant documents.  The systematic search process was carried out by following the steps shown in Figure 1.

To ensure the robustness of the findings, the quality of the 29 selected articles was assessed based on several standard criteria in SLR research. This quality assessment aims to evaluate the methodological rigor and contribution of each study. The assessment criteria used include: (a) Clarity of Research Objectives, i.e. whether the objectives and research questions of each article are clearly defined; (b) Methodological Suitability, i.e. whether the method used is appropriate to answer the research question of the article; (c) Robustness of Findings, i.e. whether the conclusions drawn are strongly supported by the data and analysis presented; and (d) Significant Contribution, i.e. the extent to which the article provides new and relevant insights into the topic of SMA, Big Data, and AI integration. All 29 articles included in this review were considered to have met adequate quality standards for synthesis. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION

Research Results

A systematic analysis of 29 relevant articles revealed that the integration of Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) with Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has a central and multifaceted role in improving financial analysis and decision-making. The findings of the reviewed literature can be synthesized into two main interrelated roles, according to the focus of the research title: (1) Improvement of financial analysis capabilities, and (2) Improvement of the quality and transformation of the nature of strategic decision-making. The Role of Integration in Improving Financial Analysis The consistently analyzed literature shows that the synergy between SMA, Big Data, and AI significantly transforms financial analysis capabilities, making them more accurate, predictive, and efficient.

1) Increased Accuracy and Depth of Analysis: The integration of technology

allows accountants to move from sample-based analysis to full-data population analysis, thus drastically increasing accuracy (Almaqtari, 2024). By leveraging machine learning and data mining algorithms, companies can identify patterns, correlations, and anomalies that are invisible through traditional methods (Fernández-Revuelta Pérez & Romero Blasco, 2022). It has proven to be highly effective in a variety of functions, such as more precise cost estimation in complex manufacturing


<!-- Page 9 -->

industries (Fernández-Revuelta Pérez & Romero Blasco, 2022; Mattetti et al., 2022), customer profitability analysis, and more comprehensive financial risk assessment (Gu & Zhou, 2023; Yang, 2022; Ren, 2022). 2) Transformation towards Predictive and Proactive Analysis: One of the

most significant roles of this integration is the shift from historical (retrospective) analysis to predictive (prospective) analysis (Manrique Plácido et al., 2025; Abdullah et al., 2022). Big Data enables real-time data collection from a variety of sources, including external market data, operational data from sensors (IoT), and even unstructured data from social media (Ren, 2022; Gu & Zhou, 2024). AI then acts as an analysis engine to build sophisticated financial forecasting models, predict future trends, and provide early warning of potential financial risks (Theodorakopoulos et al., 2025; Gusc et al., 2022; Zhang, 2023). 3) Efficiency in Data Collection and Processing: Technologies such as cloud

accounting and Big Data platforms automate the process of collecting, cleaning, and integrating data from various separate systems (Xu et al., 2023; Bian & Bian, 2022). This automation not only reduces the time and costs associated with manual data processing but also minimizes the risk of human error, thereby increasing the reliability of data as the basis for analysis (Jia et al., 2022). As a result, analysts can dedicate more time to interpreting results and formulating strategies, rather than on repetitive data collection processes (Almaqtari, 2024). The Role of Integration in Improving Decision Making Superior financial analysis directly has implications for improving the quality and effectiveness of strategic decision-making at all levels of management.

1) Improved Quality and Decision Speed: With more accurate and timely

insights, managers can make strategic decisions more confidently and quickly (Abdullah et al., 2022). AI-based Decision Support Systems are able to present quantitative recommendations and intuitive data visualization, which makes it easier for managers to understand complex business situations and reduce reliance on intuition alone (Jia et al., 2022; Wang & Dai, 2025). This is crucial in a dynamic business environment where speed of response is a determining factor of competitive advantage (Andriushchenko et al., 2019; Pantea et al., 2024). 2) Support for Complex Strategic Decisions: This integration greatly

supports the implementation of various SMA techniques. For example, competitor data analysis, strategic pricing, and customer profitability analysis can be done with an unprecedented level of depth (Abdullah et al., 2022; Nguyen & Tran, 2024). Case studies on various industries, such as transportation, show how analytics platforms are used to optimize routes, perform predictive maintenance, and manage operational costs, all of which are complex strategic decisions (Sánchez Toledano et al., 2024).

3) Changing Natures of Decision-Making—From Answers to Critical

Questions: Some literature provides the critical perspective that the role of AI should not be viewed as a perfect "answer-giving machine" (Agbon, 2024). Instead, findings from AI are supposed to trigger a "maieutic" process, in which the output of the intelligent system becomes a spark for deeper discussions, debates, and questions among management teams (Tiitola et al., 2024). In this model, the role of humans, especially management accountants, is transformed into a "translator" or "critic" who evaluates, interprets, and challenges the results of AI analysis. This ensures that the final decision remains based on sound human judgment and a deep understanding of the context, rather than blind adherence to the algorithm's recommendations (Agbon, 2024; Samarghandi et al., 2023; Tiitola et al., 2024). Discussion

The results of the research synthesized from 29 articles conclusively show that the integration of Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) with Big Data and AI has a fundamental dual role: on the one hand as a driver of operational efficiency, and on the other hand as a catalyst for superior strategic capabilities. This discussion will interpret the findings, relate them to a broader theoretical framework, and discuss their implications for the accounting profession and management practice.

Dual Role Synthesis: Operational Efficiency and Strategic Capability

Findings from the literature highlight the existence of a duality of roles that reinforce each other. At the operational level, AI and Big Data function as efficiency agents by automating repetitive transactional tasks (Almaqtari, 2024; Wang & Dai, 2025), reduces manual errors, and speeds up the reporting cycle (Jia et al., 2022). However, these benefits go beyond just cost savings. This automation is the foundation for a second, more strategic role. By freeing human resources from low-value work, companies can empower their professionals to focus on high-value activities: in-depth analysis and strategic decision-making (Almulla et al., 2024).

In its strategic role, this integration transforms SMA from a mere framework into a vibrant and dynamic system. If SMA provides the "what" that needs to be analyzed (e.g., competitor costs, customer lifetime value), then Big Data provides its fuel (abundant raw data) and AI becomes its engine (analytical and predictive capabilities) (Abdullah et al., 2022; Fernández- Revuelta Pérez & Romero Blasco, 2022). It is this synergy that allows companies to not only understand their current position but also predict where the market is moving, providing a significant competitive advantage (Gu & Zhou, 2023).

Implications for the Accounting Profession: Towards a Human-AI Symbiosis

This transformation radically redefined the accounting profession. The results of the study clearly reject the idea that technology will completely replace humans. Instead, what emerges is a human-AI symbiosis model, where success depends on effective collaboration between the two (Samarghandi et al., 2023). The role of the accountant evolved into a "translator" or "curator" of knowledge. They must have the ability to ask AI systems the right questions, interpret often complex and non-transparent outputs, and integrate them with business judgments and strategic contexts that machines do not have.

The theoretical perspectives identified in the research results strongly support this idea. The concept of "maieutic roles" (Tiitola et al., 2024) underscores that the highest value of AI analysis is not the definitive answer, but rather its ability to provoke strategic questions and debates. Similarly, the "critical discourse" framework (Agbon, 2024) emphasizes the need for accountants to actively challenge AI-generated narratives, be aware of the potential biases contained in them, and not passively accept outputs. In this symbiosis, AI handles large-scale computing, while humans handle judgment, ethics, and strategic wisdom. Implementation Challenges as an Obstacle to Strategic Value

The discussion would not be complete without acknowledging that the road to successful integration is fraught with challenges. Findings regarding data quality issues, implementation costs, skills gaps, and ethical risks are not just technical hurdles, but strategic obstacles that can thwart entire initiatives (Theodorakopoulos et al., 2024; Pantea et al., 2024). A sophisticated predictive model will be useless if it's built on bad data. Similarly, powerful analytics tools will be wasted if there is no skilled workforce to use them effectively.

This is where the role of IT Governance becomes very vital, as Almaqtari (2024) strongly demonstrates. IT Governance serves as a framework that bridges the potential of technology and the realization of strategic value. Through good governance, companies can ensure data integrity, manage privacy and security risks, align technology investments with business goals, and proactively plan training programs to address skills gaps. In other words, IT Governance is a practical mechanism for managing ethical and technical risks raised by critical researchers (Agbon, 2024; Tiitola et al., 2024), also to ensure that technology adoption is not only efficient but also responsible and sustainable.

## CONCLUSION

This study concludes that integrating Strategic Management Accounting (SMA) with Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) marks a transformative shift in both the efficiency and strategic role of accounting within organizations. Synthesizing insights from 29 scientific articles, the research


<!-- Page 12 -->


2022

highlights two primary competitive advantages: significantly improved financial analysis—characterized by greater predictive accuracy and comprehensiveness—and more robust, rapid, and evidence-based strategic decision-making. This evolution necessitates that accountants transition from traditional data processors to strategic partners capable of interpreting AI outputs, challenging assumptions, and embedding data-driven insights into business strategies. To support this shift, organizations must invest in both technology and human capital, prioritizing digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical judgment. The study also presents an integrated framework underscoring the importance of IT Governance as a mediator to ensure the ethical and strategic alignment of Big Data and AI adoption. However, limitations such as the narrow database scope and potential selection bias indicate a need for future research to conduct longitudinal studies on the longterm impact of AI on organizational performance, the evolving role of accountants, and the development of governance frameworks for AI in accounting. Further research should also examine the adoption of these technologies by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and address how accounting education curricula can adapt to equip future professionals with the skills required for this digital transformation.
